final_candidates.decision_summary: N308 lies in the EFKYNDS N-glycosylation sequon in the head/neck region; ablating this glycan may reduce shielding of fusion-relevant surfaces and enhance G-mediated entry.
Q530 is in the stalk-proximal C-terminal segment near the F-interaction region; a basic-charge substitution could modulate F-triggering communication, but support remains speculative.

stop_reason.detail: No tool budget or rounds remain to collect further evidence, so the final Top-3 is fixed at the current glycan-removal-centric ranking.

history.rationale: Terminal residue; likely low structural impact and could slightly affect ectodomain presentation, but low expected effect on entry efficiency.
Terminal residue with low structural constraint but also low expected effect on entry efficiency; kept as a low-confidence placeholder pending structure/PLM evidence.

N308 lies in an N-D-S N-glycosylation sequon (EFKYNDS, 306-310); glycan shielding near the head/neck region often suppresses paramyxovirus attachment-protein-mediated fusion, and N-to-Q is the standard glycan-ablating, minimally perturbing substitution. Remodeling glycan shielding is one of the few mechanisms plausibly linked to increased G-mediated cell entry.

Q530 sits in the C-terminal stalk-proximal segment near the F-interaction interface; a gain-of-basic-charge substitution here could modulate F-triggering communication, though support is speculative without structural evidence from 3D11.
